Hello,

I unfortunately need to make a complaint about my delivery order. I’ve only ordered this service from Wegmans once before and I had a great experience that time, so when I was unable to go to the store in person today due to illness, I opted to use the service again. I didn’t do so lightly as it costs nearly $30 more with tipping the shopper appropriately for their service and the fees from Wegmans.

I did personal shopping for years inside a grocery store, for Instacart, and for Shipt and what I experienced today was not the standard I was taught across those platforms. No intro text from the shopper - a little nitpicky but I feel like it shows courtesy and like I’m not talking to a robot. The shopper either didn't read or access my substitutions I selected because every item he had to change he simply sent the canned “item out of stock” response and if it was an item I selected as “no substitute” he simply sent a photo of a substitute item and nothing else. I asked if he was able to see my order notes (I understand sometimes there may be app issues) and he didn’t respond, nor did he respond to any questions I asked. He also started shopping my order at 7:49pm and as of 9:44pm he is still shopping. My order window for delivery was 8pm-10pm so I hardly think he’ll make it at this rate. I understand shoppers can bundle multiple orders, but I had a reasonably sized order that should not have taken two+ hours to complete.

I know none of this is Wegmans’ fault per se, but you may want to re-evaluate the partnership with Instacart. I suggest looking into what HEB does in Texas - they have their delivery drivers separate and have HEB employees do the shops, much like your in-store pickups. This would probably mitigate the issues from the Instacart shoppers who get barely any training and zero interview process.

All in all, I’m done with this online service and I’ll seek out help from friends instead if I am too ill to get to the store. I feel resentful that I spent extra money to be disappointed. Sorry for being incredibly long-winded but I wanted to make sure the details were clear.

Please follow these troubleshooting steps to resolve the issue:

Unplug the printer and plug it back in.

Ensure the power cord is securely plugged into both the printer and an outlet.
Confirm the printer light is green.

Look for an orange pause symbol light.

Press the pause button to unpause the printer.
If this doesn’t work, the printer may be out of labels or experiencing a paper jam.

Press the yellow buttons on either side of the printer to open the lid and check:

Remove any paper jams or replace an empty label roll, if necessary.

Check the connection between the printer and the adapter (black box).

Ensure the cable is properly secured if it’s loose.
Verify that the adapter’s indicator light is green.

Unplug the adapter, plug it back in, and press the button on top.

The light on the adapter should turn blue as the adapter powers on.

Ensure the scanner is plugged into the printer.

Confirm that the scanner light is green.

Add EBT Eligibility Flag:

Retailers must update their Instacart catalog file to include an EBT eligibility flag. This flag indicates whether an item is eligible for purchase with SNAP benefits.
The flag should be a boolean value (TRUE or FALSE) to denote eligibility.

Column Placement:

The additional column for the EBT eligibility flag should be placed between the existing columns in your product file (e.g., between the "taxable" and "available" columns).

Message 4 (2025-08-07 21:38:12.000 Z):
Hi Carrie,

Apologies for the delayed response and that is a great question! I’d be happy to provide clarity on how your merchant fees are calculated.

Merchant Fees are determined based on your contract terms and include Spread. The spread is the difference between what the customer is charged on the platform (Gross Merchandise Value) and what the shopper pays at checkout in-store (POS pricing). There are multiple factors that affect spreadu such as incorrect in-store prices, sales prices, cancelled orders, etc.

However, in terms of your monthly merchant fees, here’s how it works:

Merchant Fees

Calculated as: Gross Sales Amount (GSA) × Contracted Rate.

Invoices are issued the following month for the prior month’s service period (e.g., August’s invoice is sent in September).


Spread

Formula: Spread = Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) – In store Value (POS Pricing excluding markup)

Negative Spread (Payable to Instacart): If GMV is less than POS.

Example: Customer charged $90 on platform, POS swipe $100 → Spread = -$10 → Retailer owes $10 to Instacart.


Positive Spread (Payable to Retailer): If GMV is greater than POS.

Example: Customer charged $100 on platform, POS swipe $90 → Spread = +$10 → Instacart owes $10 to Retailer.



Final Invoice

The monthly invoice reflects the net of Merchant Fees and Spread.

Positive Spread increases what is payable to you, while Negative Spread increases what is owed to Instacart.



To answer your question, your 12% markup does offset the merchant fee. However, due to the spread, retailers may still receive payable or receivable invoices depending on the spread for that month. Please let me know if you have any additional questions about your merchant fees or if you’d like further clarification on how spread impacts your monthly invoices.

Please note that our Retailer Success Team is now operating on a new ticketing system. For any future inquiries, kindly direct your requests to partnership.support@instacart.com.
